text: Ophthalmology is a discipline in clinical medicine that studies the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of diseases of the visual organs (eyeball, ocular appendages). As an independent clinical specialty, it is based on anatomy (such as the structure of the cornea, lens, and retina), physiology (visual conduction pathways), and pathology, and combines optics (such as optometry techniques), imaging (fundus OCT, UBM), and microsurgical techniques, focusing on the exploration of the mechanisms of ocular diseases and precise intervention. Modern ophthalmology has separated from the traditional "otorhinolaryngology" and has become an interdisciplinary field that integrates internal medicine (such as diabetic retinopathy), surgery (cataract surgery), and preventive medicine (myopia prevention and control).
